transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because I barely sleep in any useful way anymore. I just... I'll lie awake at night replaying client models in my head. And then, even if I do drift off, I end up waking up at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach completely tight. I just go to work every day feeling like I never actually rested at all.
Are these sleep issues and the way you're feeling in the mornings affecting your work or daily activities?

Yes, they really are. Actually, I... I recently got a formal performance warning at work. The quality of my models and presentations just keeps slipping. And outside of the office, I've basically stopped showing up for everything. I used to do some volunteer teaching, I went to yoga, and I had a book club. Those things kind of kept my life intact outside of my job, but... yeah, I just don't go to any of them anymore.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about things throughout the day?

Not really, no. I mean, I obviously think about work because of the performance warning, but it's not really... worry, exactly. I'm not sitting around feeling anxious about a bunch of different things. It's more just this constant, heavy feeling. I don't really have the energy to worry, honestly. I just feel completely drained.
Do you experience any physical symptoms like headaches or muscle tension during the day?

No, not really. I don't get headaches. I mean, my stomach is tight when I wake up, like I mentioned, but during the day... no, I haven't noticed any muscle tension or anything like that. I just feel physically heavy and tired, but nothing actually hurts.
Have you experienced any changes in your appetite or interest in activities you used to enjoy?

Well, like I said a minute ago, I've pretty much lost interest in everything. The yoga, the volunteering, the book club... I just don't care about doing any of it anymore. As for my appetite... I don't know, I guess it's about the same. I haven't really noticed a change there. I just eat because I have to.
You mentioned you've lost interest in activities like yoga, volunteering, and your book club, but is there anything you still find pleasure in or look forward to doing?

No, not really. I can't think of anything. I don't look forward to weekends or seeing friends or anything like that anymore. It's just... I just go through the motions of getting through the day, and then I go to sleep. There's nothing that I actually enjoy doing right now.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It's been about three years now. It started right around the time the merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division at work. I've just felt this way ever since.
Have you ever felt significantly better for an extended period since you started feeling this way about three years ago?
No, I haven't. It's just been a constant low. I haven't had any breaks from it where I felt like my old self again, not even for a few weeks. It's just been this same feeling the whole time.
Are there any activities or things that you used to enjoy, but now don't find pleasure in, besides the ones you've already mentioned?

No, not really. Those were the main things I did outside of work. Um... I can't think of anything else specific. It just feels like the enjoyment has been drained out of everything across the board, really, so I just don't do much of anything anymore.
Do you still enjoy things that you normally would, like eating your favorite foods or watching your favorite movies?

No, not really. Um, I mean, I still eat, obviously, but it's just food. It doesn't really give me any satisfaction, even if it's something I used to love. And movies... I might turn the TV on, but I'm mostly just staring at it. I don't really get pulled into the story or feel entertained anymore. It's all just kind of flat.
Have you had any thoughts of not wanting to be alive or wishing you could just disappear?

No, I haven't. Um... I don't have any thoughts about dying or hurting myself, if that's what you mean. It's definitely a miserable feeling, being this down all the time, but I don't want to not be alive. I just... I'm just tired of it being like this.
Are there any small pleasures in life that you still enjoy?

No, I can't really think of any. Um... it's like I was saying with the food and the movies, even the little things just don't register for me right now. A nice day outside or a good cup of coffee... I just don't feel any joy from them anymore. I just sort of go through the motions.
Have you had any periods where your symptoms went away for a while, even if they came back later?

No, I haven't. Um... it's really just been constant. I can't think of a time where it lifted or went away, even for a little bit. It's just... it's always there, every day. I haven't had any kind of break from it.
Would you say that your low mood is present most of the day?

Yes, definitely. Most days, I just move through the office, and even my apartment, with this heavy, gray feeling. It's like I'm just going through the motions all day long. Honestly, it's there so much of the time that I'm often just trying not to cry when someone asks me a normal, everyday question.
Has this low mood you're describing been continuous for the past two years or more?

Yes, it has. Actually, it's been going on for about three years now. Um... it started right around the time a merger reorganized our Caribbean-market division at work. It's just been constant ever since then.
